about: LDECC and LOAD against their authors' code on the models their papers plant, with global PC read at the pair beside them; the release summary's LDECC and LOAD entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with ldecc reading its authors' code's five steps and local_optimal_adjustment's conflict rule, as merged in this change)
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey, the authors' code, and Andrey's PC ran in separate jobs of one campaign on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (20 datasets, seeds 0-19, one treatment-outcome pair each): per dataset D = Andrey's error minus the authors' code's on the same data; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly above 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly below, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on a measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree. The floor: per dataset, the error minus the empty adjustment set's (for LOAD's set, the set's missing plus extra members against the empty set's, an answer with no set counting as the empty set); it applies where the authors' code's interval lies wholly below 0, and a row then passes when Andrey's does too
error_metric: LDECC: family_error, 1 when the parent sets returned are not the family of the treatment's parent sets the true CPDAG allows; recall_loss, 1 when the treatment's true parents are not among them; hausdorff_mse, the squared Hausdorff distance of the effects estimated with the sets from the population effects of the family, in standard deviations; effect_error, the mean absolute error of the estimated effects on a fresh sample. LOAD: set_f1_loss, 1 minus the F1 of the returned set against the optimal adjustment set for the pair asked (no set counts F1 0); effect_error as for LDECC
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. Fisher's z at the authors' levels: LDECC 0.01 x 32,000 / rows (its notebooks), LOAD 0.01; both arms uncapped in tests (LDECC's paper capped its runs at 7,000 tests)
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: ldecc@<rows>: LDECC's generator (its Appendix C.1: 20 covariates, the treatment, 3 mediators, and the outcome, 25 variables); magic-niab@<rows>: the fitted MAGIC-NIAB network (44 variables), treatment G266 and outcome HT, or a pair drawn from the seed (pair=random); random-graph@10000,degree=2,nodes=<d>: LOAD's random graphs with an identifiable pair; the columns in an order drawn from the seed
gate_note: gate: the adjustment answers' correct, wrong, and incomplete counts and the net rate against the better of abstaining and the empty set (andrey_bench.local_eval.gate), for both arms; context
pareto_note: pareto: Andrey's method against global PC read at the pair (andrey.pc.adjustment) with the same test and level, effect error against seconds per fit (the PC arm does not count its tests); PC is better on both only when its paired interval lies wholly below Andrey's error and its median seconds are lower; an abstention has no effect error, so cells where PC abstains on most datasets pair fewer than 10
replay_note: replay: LDECC on its paper's own draws (its notebook's generator and seeds, 250 graphs per cell), where the columns come in the order the generator draws them; the authors' code visits variables in column order, so its numbers there also show the order, and the rows with the columns shuffled show it without; context, never judged
